questions.question_text: What percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by oceans and seas?
Which is the world's largest ocean, covering more than one-third of the planet?
Which continent is completely located in the Southern Hemisphere and permanently covered in ice?
What are micro-organisms living in oceans that produce over half of Earth's oxygen called?
Why is Earth called the 'Blue Planet'?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Approximately 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water bodies (oceans, seas, lakes). 2. When viewed from space, sunlight reflecting off the vast oceanic expanses gives Earth a vibrant blue appearance.

questions.question_text: Name the ocean named after a country and describe its strategic location.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country (India). 2. It is bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west, and Australia to the east.

questions.question_text: List the seven continents in order of land area and briefly describe the unique geographical features of Asia and Africa.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Seven Continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia. 2. Asia: Largest continent, contains the Himalayas, Mount Everest, and more than half of the human population. 3. Africa: Second largest continent, crossed by Equator, Tropic of Cancer, and Tropic of Capricorn; contains the Sahara Desert and Nile River.

questions.question_text: Source Analysis: Marine scientists report that plastic pollution in oceans breaks down into microplastics ingested by fish. Explain how oceanic plastic pollution affects marine food webs and human health.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Plastic litter thrown on land washes through rivers into oceans, breaking into tiny non-biodegradable particles (microplastics). 2. Marine organisms like fish and turtles mistake microplastics for food, suffering internal damage. 3. Toxins accumulate up the marine food chain and enter human diet when seafood is consumed.

questions.question_text: Which ocean is 'S' shaped and flanked by the Americas to the west and Europe/Africa to the east?
Which single combined landmass comprises Europe and Asia?
What is the largest island in the world?
Undersea earthquakes or volcanic eruptions trigger destructive ocean waves called:
Explain why the Northern Hemisphere is called the 'Land Hemisphere'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. More than 67% of the Earth's total land area (Asia, Europe, North America, parts of Africa) is concentrated north of the Equator. 2. In contrast, the Southern Hemisphere is dominated by vast oceanic water expanses.

questions.question_text: What is the Southern Ocean and where is it located?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The Southern Ocean (Antarctic Ocean) surrounds the continent of Antarctica. 2. It extends northwards up to 60° South latitude where its cold waters merge with the Pacific, Atlantic, and Indian Oceans.

questions.question_text: Explain the role of oceans as the 'planet's lungs' and drivers of the global water cycle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Oxygen Production: Marine phytoplankton (microscopic algae) perform photosynthesis, producing over 50% of the atmospheric oxygen humans breathe. 2. Climate Regulation: Oceans absorb heat from the Sun and distribute it across the globe via ocean currents. 3. Water Cycle: Evaporation from warm ocean surfaces creates water vapor that turns into clouds and rain, sustaining agriculture on land.

questions.question_text: Case Study (2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami): On 26 December 2004, a major undersea earthquake off Sumatra caused a devastating tsunami. Explain how NDMA and early warning systems now protect coastal communities.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Cause: Tectonic plate displacement under the seabed generates high-speed deep-water waves that rise dramatically near shallow coastlines. 2. Early Warning: Modern buoy sensors in the Indian Ocean detect seismic waves instantly and transmit alerts to emergency centers. 3. NDMA Protocols: India's National Disaster Management Authority trains coastal populations in evacuation and maintains coastal shelter belts.

questions.question_text: Which continent is also known as the 'Island Continent'?
Which is the smallest ocean in the world surrounding the North Pole?
Which mountain range separates Europe from Asia?
India's permanent research stations in Antarctica are named:
Differentiate between an Island and a Isthmus.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. An Island is a landmass completely surrounded by water on all sides (e.g., Greenland, Sri Lanka). 2. An Isthmus is a narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses and separating two bodies of water (e.g., Isthmus of Panama).

questions.question_text: What is the Mariana Trench and where is it located?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The Mariana Trench is the deepest known oceanic trench on Earth (nearly 11,000 meters deep). 2. It is located in the western Pacific Ocean.

questions.question_text: Describe the main geographical characteristics of North America and South America, including key landforms.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. North America: Third largest continent; features Rocky Mountains in the west, Appalachian Mountains in the east, and Great Lakes. Linked to South America by the Isthmus of Panama. 2. South America: Fourth largest continent; located mostly in Southern Hemisphere. Home to the Andes (world's longest mountain range) and the Amazon River (world's largest river by water volume).

questions.question_text: Environmental Focus: Why is overfishing a serious threat to ocean ecosystems, and what measures promote sustainable fishing?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Threat: Industrial overfishing depletes fish populations faster than they can reproduce, disrupting marine food webs and endangering species. 2. Solutions: Enforcing fishing quotas, establishing Marine Protected Areas (MPAs), banning destructive bottom trawling, and encouraging seasonal fishing bans during breeding periods.

questions.question_text: Which narrow passage of water connects two large water bodies like oceans or seas?
Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
The longest river in the world, the Nile, is located on which continent?
Which two island groups form India's island territories in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal?
Explain what a Peninsula is and give an example from India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. A Peninsula is a landmass surrounded by water on three sides and connected to a larger mainland on the fourth side. 2. Peninsular India is bounded by the Arabian Sea to the west, Bay of Bengal to the east, and Indian Ocean to the south.

questions.question_text: Why does Antarctica have no permanent human settlements?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent, completely covered by thick ice sheets year-round. 2. Extreme freezing temperatures make agriculture impossible, limiting human presence to scientific research stations.

questions.question_text: Explain how human activities on land directly impact oceanic health, citing three examples.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Agricultural Runoff: Fertilizers carried by rivers trigger algal blooms that create oxygen-depleted 'dead zones' in ocean waters. 2. Industrial & Domestic Sewage: Untreated waste pollutes coastal habitats, harming coral reefs and fish hatcheries. 3. Plastic Waste: Millions of tonnes of plastic trash choke marine life and disrupt ocean ecosystems.

questions.question_text: Case Analysis: Compare the geographical features of the Pacific Ocean and the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Pacific Ocean: Almost circular in shape, largest and deepest ocean, surrounded by the 'Ring of Fire' volcanic zone. 2. Atlantic Ocean: 'S' shaped, second largest ocean, highly indented coastline providing ideal sites for natural harbors and busy commercial trade routes.

questions.question_text: What is the world's longest continental mountain range located in South America?
The Arctic Ocean is connected to the Pacific Ocean by a narrow strait called:
Which continent is bounded by the Atlantic Ocean to the west, Arctic Ocean to the north, and Mediterranean Sea to the south?
Which Vedic prayer line mentioned in the text expresses reverence for water and oceans?
Define Coral Reefs and explain why they are called the 'rainforests of the sea'.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Coral Reefs are underwater structures built by tiny calcium-secreting marine organisms (corals). 2. They support immense biodiversity, providing habitat and shelter for over 25% of all marine species despite occupying under 1% of the ocean floor.

questions.question_text: What is the Antarctic Treaty System?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Signed in 1959, it is an international agreement setting aside Antarctica exclusively for peaceful scientific research. 2. It bans military activity, weapons testing, and commercial mineral mining on the continent.

questions.question_text: Describe the distribution of land and water in the Southern Hemisphere versus the Northern Hemisphere.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Northern Hemisphere: Contains over 67% of Earth's total land area, hosting major continental masses (Eurasia, North America). 2. Southern Hemisphere: Composed of 81% water, dominated by vast expanses of the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, and Southern Oceans with smaller landmasses (Australia, Antarctica, southern parts of South America and Africa).

questions.question_text: Map & Analytical Question: Identify the locations of Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar island groups relative to the Indian peninsula and describe their ecological significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Lakshadweep: Located in the Arabian Sea off the Kerala coast; composed of coral atolls with rich marine biodiversity. 2. Andaman & Nicobar Islands: Located in the Bay of Bengal; volcanic and mountainous island chains with dense tropical rainforests and strategic maritime locations.
